The lion and the tiger are the two largest members of the cat family, but they live very different lives. Lions are highly social animals. They live in groups called prides, where females often hunt together and cooperate in raising cubs. Found mainly in open grasslands and savannas, lions rely on teamwork and strong social bonds for survival. Male lions are also distinguished by their manes, a feature unique among big cats. Tigers, by contrast, are solitary animals. They prefer forests, wetlands, and areas with dense cover, spending most of their lives alone except during mating or while raising their young. Tigers are generally larger than lions on average and are excellent swimmers. Their striped coats help them blend into their surroundings, making them highly effective ambush predators. While both are apex predators, lions draw strength from cooperation and group living, whereas tigers rely on independence, stealth, and self-reliance. Each represents a different path to survival in the wild. #Lions #Tigers #Wildlife #AnimalFacts #Nature
